usecases.title: "Software for an audience of one" — hyper-personal micro-apps
usecases.summary: People vibe-code apps no company would ever ship because the market is exactly one household: a 'Tinder for dinner' decision app for a family with ADHD, a shopping list sorted by their specific grocery store's aisle order, a treadmill remote wired to Google Maps Street View.
usecases.example: A WHOOP-band tracker that correlates heart-rate spikes with calendar events to rank coworkers by how much stress they cause.

recipe.how: Pick one household annoyance and describe the app you wish existed in a short brief: who uses it, the one screen it needs, what data it holds. Let Claude Code scaffold it as a static web app, then iterate by actually using it for a week and telling Claude what annoyed you.

usecases.title: Life admin & computer janitor work
usecases.summary: Pointing Claude Code at your home directory to rename tax invoices to a consistent format, find duplicate files, organize downloads, batch-convert media, and diagnose a slow Mac. It runs locally with file access, so it handles tedious work chat-based AI can't touch.
usecases.example: Auto-renaming invoices to 'YYYY-MM-DD Vendor - Invoice - Product.pdf' across a messy folder.

recipe.how: Run claude in the messy directory and ask it to inventory the chaos first — a report, no changes. Then approve a naming/folder scheme and let it execute, moving anything questionable to a staging folder instead of deleting.

usecases.title: Indie hacking: shipping revenue-generating products fast
usecases.summary: Vibe coding went mainstream in 2026: one indie hacker built TrendFeed in 4 days and hit $12K revenue in month one; another reached $62K MRR in under 90 days. Freelancers report shipping client apps in 8 hours instead of 80.
usecases.example: Anthropic's own head of Claude Code runs five parallel sessions and hasn't hand-written code in months.

recipe.how: Pick one painful niche task people already pay to avoid. Build the smallest sellable version with Claude Code in days, not weeks; launch where that niche already gathers; reinvest feedback into weekly iterations.

usecases.title: Non-engineer knowledge work: research, hiring, and sales pipelines
usecases.summary: PMs, recruiters, and founders synthesize hundreds of customer-call transcripts to validate product assumptions, mine GitHub for qualified sales leads, generate hiring plans and interview rubrics — long-running tasks over big piles of files that a chat window chokes on.
usecases.example: Analyzing your own meeting recordings to spot patterns like conflict avoidance.

recipe.how: Export transcripts, notes, or call recordings into one folder and ask Claude Code to synthesize themes with supporting quotes into a summary doc. Refine with follow-up questions in the same session rather than starting over.

usecases.title: Creative media projects: audiobooks, games, and extending Claude itself
usecases.summary: Standout: Alexandria, an open-source tool that turns any e-book into a fully voiced multi-cast audiobook — an LLM annotates speakers and delivery directions, local TTS performs it, voice cloning included. Also popular: retro 2D games and custom MCP servers.
usecases.example: Alexandria converts epub/txt/md into multi-voice audiobooks entirely locally, exporting MP3/M4B.

recipe.how: Start from an existing open-source project (like Alexandria) or ask Claude Code to scaffold the pipeline: parse the source material, add an LLM annotation pass for structure, then render with a local engine (TTS, canvas, game loop). Keep it all local.
tools: a local TTS engine or HTML canvas

usecases.title: Selling the meta-layer: Claude Skills bundles and productized services
usecases.summary: The purest money play isn't building apps — it's selling Claude expertise. One creator made $5K+ in 50 days packaging Claude Skills bundles (SEO writer, thumbnail designer) at ~$99; productized 'AI advisor' services reportedly run up to $30K+/month. Treat income claims with normal skepticism.
usecases.example: A ~20-skill bundle sold as a $99 digital product, built by voice-transcribing domain knowledge into the skill-creator skill.

recipe.how: Voice-note your domain expertise into Claude and ask the skill-creator to package it as a reusable skill. Bundle 10-20 related skills around one audience, then list the bundle on Gumroad with a short demo video.
